introduction: This spec defines the secrets and variables subsystem for af-hub, covering database schema, store layer, REST API endpoints, variable resolution logic, PAT permission scopes, and cascading deletion. Note: requirements referencing apikit permission registry APIs are based on PRD descriptions and should be cross-checked against the installed apikit library before implementation.

glossary.DELETE /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets/:key: Endpoint to delete an org-scoped secret
glossary.DELETE /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars/:key: Endpoint to delete an org-scoped variable
glossary.DELETE /api/v1/user/secrets/:key: Endpoint to delete a user-scoped secret
glossary.DELETE /api/v1/user/vars/:key: Endpoint to delete a user-scoped variable
glossary.DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets/: Endpoint to delete a workspace-scoped secret
glossary.DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/:ke: Endpoint to delete a workspace-scoped variable
glossary.GET /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets: Endpoint to list org-scoped secret names and timestamps
glossary.GET /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars: Endpoint to list org-scoped variables with values
glossary.GET /api/v1/user/secrets: Endpoint to list user-scoped secret names and timestamps
glossary.GET /api/v1/user/vars: Endpoint to list user-scoped variables with values
glossary.GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets: Endpoint to list workspace-scoped secret names and timestamps
glossary.GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars: Endpoint to list workspace-scoped variables with values
glossary.GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolv: Endpoint returning the merged set of variables for a workspace context, applying resolution order across user, org, and workspace tiers
glossary.PAT: Personal Access Token — a scoped credential that requires explicit permission scopes for each operation
glossary.PATCH /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets/:key: Endpoint to update an org-scoped secret value
glossary.PATCH /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars/:key: Endpoint to update an org-scoped variable value
glossary.PATCH /api/v1/user/secrets/:key: Endpoint to update a user-scoped secret value
glossary.PATCH /api/v1/user/vars/:key: Endpoint to update a user-scoped variable value
glossary.PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets/:: Endpoint to update a workspace-scoped secret value
glossary.PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/:key: Endpoint to update a workspace-scoped variable value
glossary.POST /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets: Endpoint to create one or more org-scoped secrets
glossary.POST /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars: Endpoint to create one or more org-scoped variables
glossary.POST /api/v1/user/secrets: Endpoint to create one or more user-scoped secrets
glossary.POST /api/v1/user/vars: Endpoint to create one or more user-scoped variables
glossary.POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets: Endpoint to create one or more workspace-scoped secrets
glossary.POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars: Endpoint to create one or more workspace-scoped variables
glossary.anti-enumeration: Security pattern where non-existent and unauthorized resources both return HTTP 404 to prevent resource discovery by unauthorized callers
glossary.apikit: The hub's HTTP framework and permission registry library built on Echo v4
glossary.base64-encoded: Values stored in the database are encoded using standard base64; the API transparently encodes on write and decodes on read
glossary.cascading deletion: The requirement that when a user, org, or workspace is deleted, all associated secrets and variables are deleted within the same database transaction
glossary.entries: Array field in POST request bodies containing one or more key/value objects to create in a single request
glossary.org_id: The UUID of the organization that owns a workspace, stored in the workspaces table; may be null if the workspace has no org
glossary.origin: Field in the resolved variables response indicating which tier (user, org, or workspace) a resolved variable's value came from
glossary.owner_id: The identifier of the owning entity: a user UUID for owner_type='user', an org UUID for owner_type='org', or a workspace slug for owner_type='workspace'
glossary.owner_type: Discriminator column in the secrets/variables tables; one of 'user', 'org', or 'workspace'
glossary.per-scope limit: The maximum of 100 secrets or 100 variables allowed per (owner_type, owner_id) combination
glossary.resolution order: The priority ordering for variable merging: workspace (highest) > org > user (lowest); more specific scopes override less specific ones
glossary.secrets: Sensitive key/value pairs (API tokens, certificates, connection strings) stored per owner scope; values are never returned to external API clients
glossary.secrets table: SQLite table storing sensitive key/value pairs with composite primary key (owner_type, owner_id, key)
glossary.secrets:delete: PAT permission scope granting delete access to secrets
glossary.secrets:list: PAT permission scope granting list access to secret names (values never returned)
glossary.secrets:manage: PAT permission scope granting create, list, update, and delete access to secrets; implies secrets:list, secrets:write, and secrets:delete
glossary.secrets:write: PAT permission scope granting update access to existing secret values
glossary.serialized write mode: SQLite's WAL or exclusive locking mode used by hub that serializes all concurrent writes, making count-check-then-insert effectively atomic
glossary.user_id: The UUID of the user who owns a workspace, stored in the workspaces table
glossary.variables: Non-sensitive configuration key/value pairs stored per owner scope; values are readable by API clients
glossary.variables table: SQLite table storing non-sensitive key/value pairs with composite primary key (owner_type, owner_id, key)
glossary.vars:delete: PAT permission scope granting delete access to variables
glossary.vars:manage: PAT permission scope granting create, list, read, update, and delete access to variables; implies vars:read, vars:write, and vars:delete
glossary.vars:read: PAT permission scope granting list and read access to variable values
glossary.vars:write: PAT permission scope granting list, read, and update access to variable values; implies vars:read
glossary.workspaces store: The store layer component from spec 01_workspaces that provides workspace lookup including org_id and user_id fields
glossary.workspaces:read: Existing apikit PAT permission scope that grants read access to workspaces. Referenced here in the context of ownership authorization checks (non-overlapping with secrets/variables scopes).
glossary.workspaces:write: Existing apikit PAT permission scope that grants write access to workspaces. Referenced here in the context of ownership authorization checks (non-overlapping with secrets/variables scopes).
glossary.workspaces:delete: Existing apikit PAT permission scope that grants delete access to workspaces. Referenced here in the context of ownership authorization checks (non-overlapping with secrets/variables scopes).

requirements.title: Database Schema for Secrets and Variables Tables

user_story.goal: have a well-defined SQLite schema for secrets and variables
user_story.benefit: the store layer can persist and retrieve key/value pairs with correct ownership and timestamps

acceptance_criteria.action: maintains a `secrets table` and a `variables table`, each with columns owner_type (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('user','org','workspace')), `owner_id` (TEXT NOT NULL), key (TEXT NOT NULL), value (TEXT NOT NULL), created_at (TEXT NOT NULL RFC 3339), updated_at (TEXT NOT NULL RFC 3339), and a composite PRIMARY KEY of (`owner_type`, `owner_id`, key)
stores values as `base64-encoded` strings in both tables, with encoding performed transparently by the store layer before write and decoding performed transparently on read

enforces no database-level foreign key constraints on `owner_id`; referential integrity is enforced at the application layer via `cascading deletion` within the same transaction as parent resource deletion

edge_cases.action: returns an internal error to the caller rather than returning a garbled decoded value
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, error) to the calling handler, which responds with HTTP 500
edge_cases.error_condition: a value written to the database is not valid base64 on read (data corruption)

edge_cases.action: rolls back the migration transaction and leaves the database in its prior state, returning an error to the startup routine
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a non-nil error; hub startup aborts
edge_cases.error_condition: the migration to create the `secrets table` or `variables table` fails partway through

user_story.goal: receive a clear error when I submit an invalid key name
user_story.benefit: I can correct my request before any data is written

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts keys that contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, do not start with a digit, and are at most 255 characters long; enforces case-insensitive uniqueness within a scope
rejects the entire request before writing any entries
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body describing the invalid key
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a submitted key contains characters other than alphanumeric or underscore, starts with a digit, or exceeds 255 characters

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a descriptive error message
edge_cases.error_condition: a key is exactly 256 characters long (one over the limit)

edge_cases.action: accepts the key as valid
edge_cases.return_contract: proceeds with the request normally; returns HTTP 201 or HTTP 200 as appropriate
edge_cases.trigger: a key is exactly 255 characters long (at the limit) and otherwise valid

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a descriptive error message
edge_cases.error_condition: a key is an empty string

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a descriptive error message
edge_cases.error_condition: a key starts with a digit (e.g., '1_KEY')

edge_cases.action: rejects the request without writing any entries
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 409 with a JSON error body indicating the key already exists
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request contains a key that already exists at the same (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope in a prior request (cross-request duplicate)

user_story.goal: store values up to 256 KB including empty strings and multi-line content
user_story.benefit: I can manage certificates, YAML files, and feature-flag variables without worrying about encoding

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts raw values of 0 bytes (empty string) up to 262144 bytes (256 KB), encodes them as `base64-encoded` strings before storage, and decodes them transparently on read so that API clients always see raw values
rejects the entire request before writing any entries
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body describing the value size violation
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: a submitted raw value exceeds 262144 bytes

edge_cases.action: accepts the empty string and overwrites the existing stored value with an empty `base64-encoded` string
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the updated entry; for variables, value field is empty string; for secrets, value field is omitted
edge_cases.trigger: a PATCH request body contains an empty string value ("")

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating the value field is required
edge_cases.error_condition: a PATCH request body omits the value field entirely or sets it to null

edge_cases.action: accepts the value and stores it as a `base64-encoded` string
edge_cases.return_contract: proceeds normally; returns HTTP 201 or HTTP 200 as appropriate
edge_cases.trigger: a value is exactly 262144 bytes (at the 256 KB limit)

edge_cases.action: encodes the value as `base64-encoded` before storage and decodes it on read, preserving all newlines and special characters
edge_cases.return_contract: the decoded value returned to the client is byte-for-byte identical to the submitted value
edge_cases.trigger: a value contains multi-line content such as a PEM certificate or YAML document

user_story.goal: enforce a cap of 100 entries per owner scope
user_story.benefit: the database does not accumulate unbounded rows per owner

acceptance_criteria.action: counts existing entries for that scope, checks that existing count plus the number of new entries in the request does not exceed 100, and if the limit would be exceeded rejects the entire request before writing any entries
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with the message "maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded"; no entries are written
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request is received for a given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

acceptance_criteria.action: performs the count check and INSERT within the same write transaction, relying on SQLite's `serialized write mode` to ensure atomicity so that no two concurrent POST requests can simultaneously pass the count check and both push a scope past 100 entries

edge_cases.action: accepts the request and writes all entries
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with the created entries
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request would bring the scope to exactly 100 entries

edge_cases.action: rejects the entire request before writing any entries
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with the message "maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded"
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request would bring the scope to 101 entries (one over the limit)

edge_cases.action: rejects the entire request atomically; no partial writes occur
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with the message "maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded"
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request contains entries that would individually be valid but collectively push the scope over 100

user_story.goal: receive an immediate error if my POST entries array contains duplicate keys
user_story.benefit: I know my request was rejected cleanly before any data was written

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the entire request before performing any database writes
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body identifying the duplicate key
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request's `entries` array contains two or more objects with the same key (compared case-insensitively)

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request before performing any database writes
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating the entries array must not be empty
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request's `entries` array is empty

edge_cases.action: treats them as duplicates and rejects the entire request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body identifying the duplicate key
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request contains entries with keys that differ only by case (e.g., 'DB_HOST' and 'db_host')

edge_cases.action: proceeds past duplicate detection and continues with remaining validations
edge_cases.return_contract: does not return HTTP 400 for duplicate key reasons; proceeds to other validation steps
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request contains a single entry with a valid key

user_story.goal: register 8 new PAT permission scopes with apikit's permission registry
user_story.benefit: PAT holders can be granted fine-grained access to secrets and variables operations

acceptance_criteria.action: registers `secrets:manage`, `secrets:list`, `secrets:write`, and `secrets:delete` scopes with apikit, where `secrets:manage` implies `secrets:list`, `secrets:write`, and `secrets:delete`

registers `vars:manage`, `vars:read`, `vars:write`, and `vars:delete` scopes with apikit, where `vars:manage` implies `vars:read`, `vars:write`, and `vars:delete`, and `vars:write` implies `vars:read`
registers all 8 scopes independently of the workspace scopes (`workspaces:read`, `workspaces:write`, `workspaces:delete`) registered by the workspace_write_delete spec; the two sets do not overlap

edge_cases.action: returns the error to the hub startup routine
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a non-nil error; hub startup aborts
edge_cases.error_condition: apikit's permission registry returns an error when registering any of the 8 scopes (e.g., duplicate registration)

edge_cases.action: rejects the request because creation requires `secrets:manage`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body indicating insufficient scope
edge_cases.trigger: a PAT with only `secrets:list` attempts to create a secret

requirements.title: Authorization Model for Secrets and Variables Endpoints

user_story.goal: have my access to secrets and variables governed by my token type and scope
user_story.benefit: sensitive data is protected and access is appropriately restricted

acceptance_criteria.action: grants admin tokens full access to all secrets and variables endpoints at any scope without ownership checks
grants API keys implicit full access to secrets and variables owned by the authenticated user, their org memberships, and their workspaces, including `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved`
enforces the required permission scope for each endpoint as defined in the REST API endpoint tables; a PAT lacking the required scope is rejected
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body indicating the missing scope
acceptance_criteria.state: the request is authenticated with a PAT

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a request targets an org-scoped endpoint and the authenticated caller is not a member of that org

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a request targets a workspace-scoped endpoint and the authenticated caller does not own that workspace

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 401 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: an unauthenticated request (no token) reaches any secrets or variables endpoint

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration` regardless of the PAT scope
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a PAT with `secrets:manage` attempts to access an org-scoped endpoint for an org the PAT holder is not a member of

edge_cases.action: grants access because `vars:write` implies `vars:read`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the variable list
edge_cases.trigger: a PAT with `vars:write` attempts to list variables

user_story.goal: create one or more secrets at a given ownership scope in a single request
user_story.benefit: I can batch-create secrets efficiently without multiple round trips

acceptance_criteria.action: validates all entries (key naming, value size, intra-request duplicates, scope limit), encodes values as `base64-encoded` strings, writes all entries atomically, and returns the created entries without values
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with a JSON array of objects each containing key, created_at, and updated_at; the value field is never included in the response
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request is made to `POST /api/v1/user/secrets`, `POST /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets`, or `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets` with a valid `entries` array

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the entire request without writing any entries
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 409 with a JSON error body indicating the key already exists
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request to a secrets endpoint contains a key that already exists at the same (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request to `POST /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets` references an org slug that does not exist

edge_cases.action: rolls back the transaction and returns an error to the caller
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500 with a JSON error body; no entries are persisted
edge_cases.error_condition: the database write fails after validation passes (e.g., disk full or SQLite error)

edge_cases.action: rejects the request because creation requires `secrets:manage`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request to a secrets endpoint is made by a PAT with `secrets:list` but not `secrets:manage`

user_story.role: API client with secrets:list or secrets:manage scope
user_story.goal: list secret names and timestamps at a given ownership scope
user_story.benefit: I can audit which secrets exist without ever seeing their values

acceptance_criteria.action: retrieves all secrets for the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope and returns them sorted alphabetically ascending by key (case-insensitive), never including values
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of objects each containing key, created_at, and updated_at; the value field is never included
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request is made to `GET /api/v1/user/secrets`, `GET /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets`, or `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets`

acceptance_criteria.action: returns an empty array
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array []
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request is made to a secrets list endpoint for a scope with no secrets

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a GET request to `GET /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets` references an org the caller is not a member of

edge_cases.action: rejects the request because listing requires `secrets:manage` or `secrets:list`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.trigger: a GET request to a secrets list endpoint is made by a PAT with `secrets:write` but not `secrets:list` or `secrets:manage`

user_story.role: API client with secrets:write or secrets:manage scope
user_story.goal: update the value of an existing secret at a given ownership scope
user_story.benefit: I can rotate credentials without deleting and recreating the secret

acceptance_criteria.action: validates the value, encodes it as `base64-encoded`, updates the stored value and updated_at timestamp, and returns the updated entry without the value
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing key, created_at, and updated_at; the value field is never included
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a PATCH request is made to `PATCH /api/v1/user/secrets/:key`, `PATCH /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets/:key`, or `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets/:key` with a valid value field

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the key specified in the PATCH path does not exist at the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating the value field is required
edge_cases.error_condition: the PATCH request body omits the value field or sets it to null

edge_cases.action: performs a case-insensitive lookup and updates the matching entry
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the updated entry using the originally stored key casing
edge_cases.trigger: a PATCH request to a secrets endpoint uses a key that differs in case from the stored key (e.g., PATCH 'db_host' when stored as 'DB_HOST')

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body describing the value size violation
edge_cases.error_condition: the new value in the PATCH request exceeds 262144 bytes

user_story.role: API client with secrets:delete or secrets:manage scope
user_story.goal: delete a secret at a given ownership scope
user_story.benefit: I can remove credentials that are no longer needed

acceptance_criteria.action: deletes the secret with the given key at the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 204 No Content
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a DELETE request is made to `DELETE /api/v1/user/secrets/:key`, `DELETE /api/v1/orgs/:slug/secrets/:key`, or `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets/:key`

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the key specified in the DELETE path does not exist at the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

edge_cases.action: performs a case-insensitive lookup and deletes the matching entry
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 204 No Content
edge_cases.trigger: a DELETE request to a secrets endpoint uses a key that differs in case from the stored key

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a DELETE request to `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets/:key` is made by a PAT with `secrets:delete` for a workspace the PAT holder does not own

user_story.goal: create one or more variables at a given ownership scope in a single request
user_story.benefit: I can batch-create configuration variables efficiently

acceptance_criteria.action: validates all entries (key naming, value size, intra-request duplicates, scope limit), encodes values as `base64-encoded` strings, writes all entries atomically, and returns the created entries including decoded values
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 201 with a JSON array of objects each containing key, value (decoded), created_at, and updated_at
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request is made to `POST /api/v1/user/vars`, `POST /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars`, or `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars` with a valid `entries` array

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the entire request without writing any entries
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 409 with a JSON error body indicating the key already exists
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a POST request to a variables endpoint contains a key that already exists at the same (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request to `POST /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars` references an org slug that does not exist

edge_cases.action: rolls back the transaction and returns an error to the caller
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500 with a JSON error body; no entries are persisted
edge_cases.error_condition: the database write fails after validation passes

edge_cases.action: rejects the request because creation requires `vars:manage`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.trigger: a POST request to a variables endpoint is made by a PAT with `vars:read` but not `vars:manage`

user_story.role: API client with vars:read, vars:write, or vars:manage scope
user_story.goal: list variables and their values at a given ownership scope
user_story.benefit: I can inspect configuration values for a given owner

acceptance_criteria.action: retrieves all variables for the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope, decodes values from `base64-encoded` storage, and returns them sorted alphabetically ascending by key (case-insensitive)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of objects each containing key, value (decoded), created_at, and updated_at
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request is made to `GET /api/v1/user/vars`, `GET /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars`, or `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars`

acceptance_criteria.action: returns an empty array
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array []
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request is made to a variables list endpoint for a scope with no variables

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a GET request to `GET /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars` references an org the caller is not a member of

edge_cases.action: rejects the request because listing requires `vars:read`, `vars:write`, or `vars:manage`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.trigger: a GET request to a variables list endpoint is made by a PAT with `vars:delete` but not `vars:read`, `vars:write`, or `vars:manage`

user_story.role: API client with vars:write or vars:manage scope
user_story.goal: update the value of an existing variable at a given ownership scope
user_story.benefit: I can change configuration values without deleting and recreating the variable

acceptance_criteria.action: validates the value, encodes it as `base64-encoded`, updates the stored value and updated_at timestamp, and returns the updated entry with the decoded value
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing key, value (decoded), created_at, and updated_at
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a PATCH request is made to `PATCH /api/v1/user/vars/:key`, `PATCH /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars/:key`, or `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/:key` with a valid value field

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the key specified in the PATCH path does not exist at the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating the value field is required
edge_cases.error_condition: the PATCH request body omits the value field or sets it to null

edge_cases.action: performs a case-insensitive lookup and updates the matching entry
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the updated entry using the originally stored key casing
edge_cases.trigger: a PATCH request to a variables endpoint uses a key that differs in case from the stored key

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body describing the value size violation
edge_cases.error_condition: the new value in the PATCH request exceeds 262144 bytes

user_story.role: API client with vars:delete or vars:manage scope
user_story.goal: delete a variable at a given ownership scope
user_story.benefit: I can remove configuration values that are no longer needed

acceptance_criteria.action: deletes the variable with the given key at the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 204 No Content
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a DELETE request is made to `DELETE /api/v1/user/vars/:key`, `DELETE /api/v1/orgs/:slug/vars/:key`, or `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/:key`

acceptance_criteria.action: rejects the request
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the key specified in the DELETE path does not exist at the given (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) scope

edge_cases.action: performs a case-insensitive lookup and deletes the matching entry
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 204 No Content
edge_cases.trigger: a DELETE request to a variables endpoint uses a key that differs in case from the stored key

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.trigger: a DELETE request to `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/:key` is made by a PAT with `vars:delete` for a workspace the PAT holder does not own

user_story.role: API client with vars:read, vars:write, or vars:manage scope
user_story.goal: retrieve the fully merged set of variables for a workspace context
user_story.benefit: I can see the effective configuration that will be applied to a workspace without manually merging three tiers

acceptance_criteria.action: looks up the workspace via the `workspaces store` to obtain `org_id` and `user_id`, fetches variables for all applicable tiers (user, org if `org_id` is non-null, workspace), merges them using `resolution order` (workspace wins over org wins over user), and returns the merged set sorted alphabetically ascending by key (case-insensitive) with an `origin` field on each entry
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of objects each containing key, value (decoded), origin (one of 'user', 'org', 'workspace'), created_at, and updated_at from the winning tier's record
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a GET request is made to `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved`

acceptance_criteria.action: skips the org tier entirely and merges only user-level and workspace-level variables
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the merged result; no org-tier variables appear
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the workspace referenced in `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` has a null or empty `org_id`

acceptance_criteria.action: uses the value from the most specific tier (workspace > org > user) and sets the `origin` field to that tier's name; timestamps are taken from the winning tier's record
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the winning tier's value, origin, created_at, and updated_at for that key
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the same key exists at multiple tiers for a workspace resolution

edge_cases.action: rejects the request using `anti-enumeration`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 404
edge_cases.error_condition: the workspace slug in `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` does not exist or the caller does not own it

edge_cases.action: returns an empty merged set
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array []
edge_cases.trigger: a GET request to `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` is made for a workspace with no variables at any tier

edge_cases.action: returns an internal error to the caller
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 500 with a JSON error body
edge_cases.error_condition: the `workspaces store` lookup fails (e.g., database error) during resolution

edge_cases.action: rejects the request
edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body

edge_cases.return_contract: returns HTTP 200 with the merged variable set

requirements.title: Cascading Deletion of Secrets and Variables

user_story.goal: ensure all secrets and variables for a deleted owner are removed in the same transaction as the parent deletion
user_story.benefit: the database never contains orphaned rows even if the process crashes between parent and child deletions

acceptance_criteria.action: deletes all rows in the `secrets table` and `variables table` where (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) matches the deleted entity, within the same database transaction as the parent resource deletion
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a user, org, or workspace is deleted

acceptance_criteria.action: wraps the parent resource deletion and the child secrets/variables deletions in a single database transaction so that either all deletions commit or none do

edge_cases.action: rolls back the entire transaction, leaving the parent resource and all its secrets/variables intact
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a non-nil error to the calling handler, which responds with HTTP 500
edge_cases.error_condition: the child secrets/variables deletion fails within the transaction (e.g., database error)

edge_cases.action: executes the deletion queries for secrets and variables (which affect 0 rows) without error and commits the transaction
edge_cases.return_contract: returns nil error; parent resource is deleted successfully
edge_cases.trigger: a user, org, or workspace with no associated secrets or variables is deleted

edge_cases.action: SQLite rolls back the uncommitted transaction on next startup, leaving both the parent resource and its secrets/variables intact
edge_cases.return_contract: no orphaned rows exist after recovery
edge_cases.error_condition: the process crashes after the parent resource deletion SQL executes but before the transaction commits

correctness_properties.title: Secret values are never returned by any API endpoint
correctness_properties.invariant: no GET, POST, PATCH, or DELETE response body for any `secrets` endpoint includes a value field; only key, created_at, and updated_at are returned

correctness_properties.title: Base64 round-trip preserves value bytes
correctness_properties.for_any: raw value V of 0 to 262144 bytes submitted to any create or update endpoint
correctness_properties.invariant: the value returned by a subsequent GET or PATCH response is byte-for-byte identical to V

correctness_properties.title: Per-scope entry count never exceeds 100
correctness_properties.for_any: (`owner_type`, `owner_id`) combination in the `secrets table` or `variables table`
correctness_properties.invariant: the number of rows with that (owner_type, owner_id) pair never exceeds 100

correctness_properties.title: Key uniqueness is case-insensitive within a scope
correctness_properties.for_any: pair of rows in the `secrets table` or `variables table` with the same (`owner_type`, `owner_id`)
correctness_properties.invariant: no two rows have keys that are equal when compared case-insensitively

correctness_properties.title: Resolution order: workspace overrides org overrides user
correctness_properties.for_any: key K present at two or more tiers for a given workspace resolution
correctness_properties.invariant: the resolved value for K is the value from the most specific tier (workspace if present, else org if present, else user), and the `origin` field reflects that tier

correctness_properties.title: List and resolved endpoints return keys in case-insensitive alphabetical order
correctness_properties.for_any: response from any GET list or `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` endpoint
correctness_properties.invariant: the keys in the response array are sorted in ascending alphabetical order when compared case-insensitively

correctness_properties.title: Cascading deletion leaves no orphaned rows
correctness_properties.for_any: user, org, or workspace that is deleted
correctness_properties.invariant: after the deletion transaction commits, no rows exist in the `secrets table` or `variables table` with an `owner_id` matching the deleted entity's identifier

correctness_properties.title: POST validation is all-or-nothing
correctness_properties.for_any: POST request to any secrets or variables create endpoint
correctness_properties.invariant: either all entries in the request are written atomically or none are; no partial writes occur regardless of which validation rule is violated

execution_paths.title: Create a workspace-scoped secret via PAT

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/secrets with Authorization header containing a PAT bearing secrets:manage scope and a JSON body with an entries array
validates the PAT, checks that it has secrets:manage scope, and verifies the caller owns the workspace; returns HTTP 403 or HTTP 404 if either check fails

validates the entries array is non-empty, checks for intra-request duplicate keys (case-insensitive), validates each key against naming rules, and validates each value does not exceed 262144 bytes; returns HTTP 400 if any check fails

opens a write transaction, counts existing secrets for (owner_type='workspace', owner_id=slug), checks that count + new entries <= 100, checks for cross-request duplicate keys returning HTTP 409 if found, encodes each value as base64-encoded, inserts all rows, and commits the transaction
returns HTTP 201 with a JSON array of objects containing key, created_at, and updated_at for each created secret; value is never included

execution_paths.title: Resolve variables for a workspace context

steps.action: sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved with an Authorization header containing an API key
validates the API key and verifies the caller owns the workspace; returns HTTP 404 if the workspace does not exist or is not owned by the caller
calls the workspaces store to look up the workspace record and retrieve org_id and user_id
returns the workspace record including org_id (may be null) and user_id

fetches all variables for owner_type='user' and owner_id=user_id; fetches all variables for owner_type='org' and owner_id=org_id (skipped if org_id is null); fetches all variables for owner_type='workspace' and owner_id=slug; decodes all values from base64-encoded storage

merges the three variable sets using resolution order (workspace overrides org overrides user), attaches the origin field to each entry, sorts the result alphabetically ascending by key (case-insensitive)
returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of resolved variable objects each containing key, value, origin, created_at, and updated_at from the winning tier's record

execution_paths.title: Delete a user and cascade-delete their secrets and variables

steps.action: initiates deletion of a user account
opens a database transaction and executes DELETE on the users table for the given user UUID
within the same transaction, executes DELETE on the secrets table WHERE owner_type='user' AND owner_id=user_uuid
within the same transaction, executes DELETE on the variables table WHERE owner_type='user' AND owner_id=user_uuid
commits the transaction; all three deletions are atomically persisted with no orphaned rows

execution_paths.title: Update a variable value via PATCH

steps.action: sends PATCH /api/v1/user/vars/:key with a JSON body containing a value field
validates the token and checks that the caller has vars:manage or vars:write scope (for PATs); returns HTTP 401 or HTTP 403 if checks fail
checks that the value field is present and not null, and that the raw value does not exceed 262144 bytes; returns HTTP 400 if either check fails
performs a case-insensitive lookup for the key at (owner_type='user', owner_id=caller_uuid); returns HTTP 404 if not found
encodes the new value as base64-encoded, updates the row's value and updated_at columns, and commits the write
returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object containing key, value (decoded), created_at, and updated_at

error_handling.condition: Invalid key name (contains non-alphanumeric/non-underscore characters, starts with a digit, or exceeds 255 characters)
error_handling.behavior: Reject the entire request before any writes; return HTTP 400 with a JSON error body describing the invalid key
Reject the entire request before any writes; return HTTP 400 with a JSON error body describing the value size violation
Reject the request before any writes; return HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating the entries array must not be empty

error_handling.condition: POST entries array contains two or more entries with the same key (case-insensitive intra-request duplicate)
error_handling.behavior: Reject the entire request before any writes; return HTTP 400 with a JSON error body identifying the duplicate key

error_handling.condition: POST would push the (owner_type, owner_id) scope past 100 entries
error_handling.behavior: Reject the entire request before any writes; return HTTP 400 with the message "maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded"

error_handling.condition: POST contains a key that already exists at the same (owner_type, owner_id) scope (cross-request duplicate)
error_handling.behavior: Reject the entire request without writing any entries; return HTTP 409 with a JSON error body indicating the key already exists

error_handling.condition: Unauthenticated request (no token) to any secrets or variables endpoint
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 401 with a JSON error body

error_handling.condition: PAT lacks the required permission scope for the requested operation
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 403 with a JSON error body indicating the missing scope

error_handling.condition: Caller is not a member of the org for an org-scoped endpoint (anti-enumeration)
Caller does not own the workspace for a workspace-scoped endpoint (anti-enumeration)
PATCH or DELETE targeting a key that does not exist at the given scope
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 404 with a JSON error body

error_handling.condition: PATCH request body omits the value field or sets it to null
error_handling.behavior: Return HTTP 400 with a JSON error body indicating the value field is required

error_handling.condition: Workspace slug in GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved does not exist or caller does not own it
Database write fails after validation passes (e.g., disk full or SQLite error)
error_handling.behavior: Roll back the transaction; return HTTP 500 with a JSON error body; no entries are persisted

error_handling.condition: Child secrets/variables deletion fails within the cascading deletion transaction
error_handling.behavior: Roll back the entire transaction leaving parent resource and all its secrets/variables intact; return a non-nil error to the calling handler which responds with HTTP 500
